title: Prefetch & pipelined KV windowing to reduce GPU oversubscription stalls
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: under oversubscribed workloads (more concurrent contexts than GPU resident KV capacity) we observe high p99 latency spikes caused by synchronous GPU page-in events and small fragmented transfers. This ticket proposes a prefetched, pipelined 'KV windowing' approach: group logical KV requests into windowed prefetch batches, schedule asynchronous DMA transfers ahead of compute, and maintain a lightweight runahead estimator per worker to avoid head-of-line blocking.
spec_notes:
Overview of solution:
- Block layout: store KV entries in fixed-size blocked pages (configurable page_size_bytes, default 256KB) with an index so adjacent entries are coalesced during prefetch.
- Windowing: each request stream maintains a sliding 'runahead window' of upcoming KV keys based on token-generation trace heuristics (prefix reuse, attention locality). The window size is dynamic: start small (4 pages) and grow to an upper bound (32 pages) as the estimator gains confidence.
- Prefetch pipeline: three stages -- (1) candidate selection (CPU), (2) transfer planning & throttling (CPU + driver), (3) async GPU DMA transfer + notification. Transfers are split into chunked 64KB segments to tolerate preemption but coalesced when possible.
- Memory pressure signal: resident_ratio = gpu_used_bytes / gpu_capacity_bytes. If resident_ratio > hard_threshold (default 0.78), prefetch aggressiveness is reduced and eviction becomes conservative. If an OOM-like event is predicted (continuous page fault spike), fall back to synchronous blocking path with explicit backoff.
- Eviction & priority buckets: pages are assigned priorities (hot/prefetch_candidate/low). Hot pages use MRU protection windows; prefetch_candidate pages are eligible for eviction after a grace period.
- Metrics & telemetry: record prefetch_hit_rate, async_transfer_bytes, sync_page_faults, prefetch_latency_ms, p99_inference_latency. Add labels to traces to correlate prefetch decisions with downstream latency.
implementation_plan:
1) Prototype user-space prefetcher as a separate module behind a feature flag. 2) Add blocked page index structures and small allocator changes to store block metadata. 3) Implement runahead estimator using exponential smoothing of sequence offsets from production traces. 4) Integrate async DMA scheduling with existing mover thread; implement chunked transfer with coalescing heuristics. 5) Add telemetry and unit+integration tests. 6) Canary rollout on dedicated pools with controlled oversubscription.
Milestones:
- Week 1: prototype index + allocator + unit tests.
- Week 2: runahead estimator + simulator against traces.
- Week 3: async transfer integration + microbenchmarks.
- Week 4: canary rollout + telemetry validation.
- Week 5: broader rollout and cleanup.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Aggressive prefetching improves p99 at the cost of extra GPU memory and PCIe bandwidth; must be throttled when other tenants exist.
- Chunked transfers avoid long blocking DMA but may increase overall bytes transferred due to header/fragmentation overhead.
- Estimators can mispredict for highly irregular / adversarial inputs; provide safe fallback to blocking path and expose config knobs.
- Complexity increases maintenance burden for allocator and eviction logic; keep default conservative and tested.
- Cross-socket NUMA effects on on-prem deployments must be evaluated (PCIe topology can change effective transfer latency).
benchmarks:
Planned benchmarks:
- Synthetic oversubscription: 32 concurrent contexts vs GPU resident capacity equal to 8 contexts. Target: reduce sync_page_faults by >= 40% and improve p99 latency by >= 15% for generation length 512.
- Production trace replay: use week-of traces from customer A and customer B; measure prefetch_hit_rate and extra bytes moved. Target: prefetch_hit_rate >= 0.65 while transfer overhead < 20% more bytes.
- Microbenchmarks for chunk size sensitivity: test 16KB/64KB/256KB chunk sizes and record transfer tail behaviour.
Link to benchmark harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/main/benchmarks/kv-prefetch
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for blocked page index and allocator changes with coverage for fragmentation scenarios
Integration test that simulates page faults and validates async DMA path correctness
Canary run shows: sync_page_faults reduced by >= 40% and p99 latency improved >= 15% under synthetic oversubscription
Telemetry events emitted for every prefetch decision and transfers visible in console dashboards
Feature gated behind 'kv_window_prefetch' flag with rollout plan and ability to disable per-customer
No regressions on baseline workloads (CPU-bound small-models) verified by CI smoke suite
rollout_plan:
- Staged rollout: feature-flagged.
- Phase 1 (internal): enable in internal test pools and run stress traces for 72 hours.
- Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5% of dedicated customers on canary cluster; monitor p99, OOM events, PCIe bandwidth.
- Phase 3 (ramped): 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 48-hour observation windows, automatic rollback on high sync_page_fault rate or elevated GPU memory churn.
- Provide per-customer knob to pin prefetch aggressiveness and page_size_bytes.
monitoring_and_alerting:
New alerts:
- prefetch_hit_rate < 0.2 for 10m => investigate estimator regressions.
- sync_page_faults increase > 2x baseline in canary => rollback.
- async_transfer_queue_growth > 1000 entries for 5m => potential PCIe saturation.
Dashboards to add: per-pool prefetch hit/miss, transfer bytes by priority, p99 latency annotated with prefetch decisions. Trace link: console.redwood.ai/dashboards/kv-prefetch
qa_tests:
- Deterministic unit tests that inject page fault callbacks and validate ordering of transfers.
- End-to-end test with a toy language model to assert throughput/latency under oversubscription.
- Fault injection: simulate failed DMA segments and ensure retry/backoff path behaves and does not deadlock.
- Stress test for 48h on internal cluster with varying request size distributions.
